column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the promised position “keeper of my head”; BSB renders the head image as “my bodyguard.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “they camped” at Gilboa after Saul gathered Israel; BSB makes Saul the continuing subject of “camped.”
The Hebrew says Saul’s heart trembled greatly; BSB makes Saul himself the subject of trembling.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul as the inquirer; BSB uses “He.”
The Hebrew describes the woman as a possessor of a spirit; BSB uses the role name “a medium.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker at the woman’s house unnamed and includes a request particle; BSB names Saul and leaves the request particle implicit.
The Hebrew uses collective singular for the spiritist and describes setting a trap for her soul. BSB uses plural “spiritists” and leaves the soul image implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the woman” before her speech; BSB combines her seeing, crying out, and speaking under one subject.
The Hebrew has a plural ascending participle with Elohim; BSB uses singular “a god coming up.”
The Hebrew leaves the questioner unnamed; BSB supplies Saul.
The Hebrew explicitly says God does not answer “by the hand of the prophets”; BSB leaves the hand image implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the LORD in the first clause and says He spoke “by my hand”; BSB uses “He” and “through me.”
The Hebrew says Saul did not listen “to the voice of the LORD”; BSB renders this as not obeying the LORD.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes Saul falling to the ground in the fullness of his height and says he had eaten no bread. BSB uses “fell flat” and had not eaten “anything.”
The Hebrew says she placed her soul in her singular palm; BSB uses “life in my hands.” It explicitly says she heard his words, where BSB says she “did as you told me.”
The Hebrew asks Saul to hear “the voice of your maidservant”; BSB leaves the voice image implicit.
The Hebrew leaves Saul unnamed as the one refusing; BSB supplies his name.
